To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Trichoderma isolates of the same species can differ considerably in their biocontrol potential; the genetic variability of T. harizanum, T. hamatum and T. virid is high, and some strains of these species can be recommended to be used as partners in strain‐improvement programmes.

the genetic diversity within the Trichodermaceae is very high and that the genetic differences between the strains of the same species are much greater than the differences between the species of the same genus.

the genetic diversity of Trichoderman strains can be used to select promising partners for breeding programmes, since their strong affinities offer the best chances for combining the contrasted biocontrol properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biological characterisation and the genetic analysis of Trichodermas as a basis for strain improvement and the development of new biological control agents.
the selection of Trichodermas with high MPA, chitinase activity, ANA and high intraspecific genetic similarity.
the development of new biocontrol agents based on Trichoderma spp.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most suitable strain for a strain breeding programme is the strain with the highest MPA and the lowest ANA.
a strain‐improved biocontrol agent should be characterised not by a single, but by multiple biocontrol traits.
the most appropriate partners of a breeding programme for a particular pathogen should be selected from among strains of the most closely related species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most promising partners for strain‐improvement are T. hamatum strains 2 and 3 and T. harziamum 1.

the genetic diversity among Trichoderma isolates is not necessarily reflected in their biocontrol potential, and that the choice of a strain for a biocontrol breeding programme is a very complex matter.
a strain‐breeders should be well aware of the diversity within species, and should choose the most appropriate strains to combine their contrasted biological and molecular characteristics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of RAPD analysis in Trichoderma research can be very useful in selecting the best strains for a breeding programme.
a strain‐improved biocontrol agent can be obtained by combining the best biocontrol traits of different Trichoderma species.
RAPD analysis can be a useful tool for the identification of strains with high potential for biocontrol.
